title: Framework for Optimising Care Using a Modular Support Package for ARFID
official: Manualisation and Feasibility Evaluation of a Modular Support Package for Children and Adolescents Living With Avoidant Restrictive Food Intake Disorder: a Single Arm Case Series
summary: ARFID (Avoidant Restrictive Food Intake Disorder) is when a person eats only a small amount of food, or only a few types of food. This makes it difficult for an individual to eat enough or have a varied, nutritional diet. This study is testing a new way of organising support for young people aged 4 to 17 with ARFID. The support is split into parts, called modules. Each young person gets the modules that fit them best. The modules use ideas that NHS teams already use. We want to find out if the support works well in the NHS, and if young people, their caregivers and clinicians like it. What they tell us will help us make it better.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Children or adolescents aged 4-17 years clinically assessed as presenting with ARFID, at ELCH or MCCAED.
* Caregivers of participating children or adolescents, who receive the manualised support package, can provide informed consent and participate in study procedures (e.g. questionnaires and interviews).
* Clinicians involved in delivering the modular support package (e.g. occupational therapists, psychologists, and speech and language therapists), who can provide informed consent, deliver the support package and participate in interviews (work phase 2).
* The study will recruit participants who are able to understand the support package content in English, either directly or with support from an interpreter.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Participants will be excluded prior or during the study if they are at high physical risk e.g. ongoing rapid weight loss.
* Children will be excluded if they are acutely unwell and require immediate hospitalisation.
* Individuals or their caregivers who do not consent to the research team contacting their GP or paediatrician regarding their participation in the study will not be eligible.
* Young people aged 16 years or older who lack capacity to provide informed consent will be excluded from the study.
* Young people and/or their caregivers will be excluded if they are unable to meaningfully engage with the support package or interviews, even with reasonable adjustments.
* The research team will attempt to be flexible in terms of session delivery, but where a family indicate they would not be available to attend any sessions, they would be excluded.
